Baker Mayfield got sacked 6 times and hit 12 times against Minnesota.

He dislocated his throwing thumb on the final drive.

He's back Sunday. His starting right tackle isn't.

Baker was never Tampa's problem. Here's why.

1. The offense was broken before he got hurt

Tampa went 0 and 3 with him. 2 TDs, 2 picks. Easy to blame the quarterback.

But look at the Minnesota game. 2 for 17 on third down. An 85 yard Chris Godwin touchdown wiped out by holding.

The hold was on Luke Goedeke. The same right tackle who's out Sunday.

2. He's walking into the same mess

First game back from a dislocated throwing thumb. Behind a line that let him get hit 12 times the last time he played. No Goedeke. No Emeka Egbuka either, who's out with a concussion and a foot injury.

That's not a comeback. That's a stress test.

3. The backup numbers tell you everything

Jalon Daniels deserves credit. He beat Dallas, still Tampa's only win this year.

But he threw 3 TDs and 5 picks while Baker was out. The Bucs went 1 and 2 in his starts.

Different quarterback. Same problems.

My call

Tampa's issue is the line, not the quarterback. If they lose Sunday, people will blame Baker. They'll be wrong.

Tell me I'm wrong.
